label: Microwave or OTG oven

questions.text: How many times a day is it used?
questions.why: Heavy use wears the heating parts and door switches.

questions.text: Which containers go in a microwave?
questions.why: Metal and some plastics can spark or melt.

questions.text: How often is the inside cleaned?
questions.why: Food splashes absorb energy and can burn.

questions.text: Does the door close firmly and the seal look clean?
questions.why: A good door seal keeps the heat and microwaves inside.

questions.text: Is there space around the vents?
Have you noticed sparks, a burning smell, or it not heating?
questions.why: Early signs let you get it checked before a small fault grows.

care_tips.text: Switch off and unplug the oven before cleaning it.
care_tips.why: Cleaning an appliance that is plugged in risks an electric shock.

care_tips.text: Don't open the oven yourself; leave repairs to the brand's authorised service.
care_tips.why: Inside there are live parts, and opening it can also end the warranty.
Running it empty can damage it.

care_tips.text: Use only microwave-safe containers and no metal in a microwave.
care_tips.why: Metal sparks and some plastics melt.

care_tips.text: Wipe the inside and the door seal regularly.
care_tips.why: Food splashes can burn and damage the cavity.

care_tips.text: If the door does not close firmly, stop using it and contact the brand's service.
care_tips.why: A poor door seal is unsafe.

care_tips.text: If it sparks, smells of burning or stops heating, unplug it and contact the brand's service.
care_tips.why: These can be signs of a dangerous fault.

reminders.text: Wipe the inside and door seal of the oven (unplugged).
reminders.note: Check your manual for the interval for your model.
